clarifiedQuestion: Of the inventory units stocked in September 2025 UTC, how many were still unsold at the close of September 30 at each recorded distribution center?
assumptions: The cutoff is the instant before October 1 UTC. A sale timestamped exactly at October 1 midnight belongs to October.
A missing sale timestamp means the unit has no recorded sale.
Each unit belongs to the distribution center recorded on its inventory row.
reasoningChain: The inventory view has one row per physical unit and records both stocking and sale times. The center lookup supplies a display name while the recorded center ID keeps centers with the same name distinct.
generatedSql:
SELECT
  i.product_distribution_center_id AS center_id,
  COALESCE(d.name, 'Unknown') AS center_name,
  COUNT(*) AS stocked_units,
  COUNTIF(i.sold_at IS NULL OR i.sold_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-10-01 00:00:00+00') AS unsold_units
FROM `tv_thelook.inventory_items` AS i
LEFT JOIN `tv_thelook.distribution_centers` AS d
  ON d.id = i.product_distribution_center_id
WHERE i.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-09-01 00:00:00+00'
  AND i.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-10-01 00:00:00+00'
GROUP BY center_id, center_name
ORDER BY unsold_units DESC, center_id ASC, center_name ASC
LIMIT 100
explanation: The synthetic Cedar Depot row shows 120 units stocked in September and 45 unsold at month-end. A unit sold on October 2 contributes to both counts because it was still unsold at the cutoff.
teachingsUsed: Reconstruct historical unsold counts by comparing the sale timestamp with the reporting cutoff.
supervisorNotes: The first draft counted only missing sale timestamps. The accepted query also counts units sold after September closed.
